articles.title: A Texas courthouse built in 1914 has sat empty since 1977 as reuse plans failed and renovation estimates reached $120 million; the county has now awarded a $1.3 million demolition contract
articles.summary: Nueces County leaders have voted unanimously to award a $1.3 million contract to demolish the historic 1914 Nueces County Courthouse in downtown Corpus
articles.body: Nueces County leaders have voted unanimously to award a $1.3 million contract to demolish the historic 1914 Nueces County Courthouse in downtown Corpus Christi. The decision brings nearly five decades of debate over the deteriorating building closer to an end. The Nueces County Commissioners Court approved a plan that allows contractors to remove asbestos and tear down the 110-year-old structure. According to reports from local television stations KRIS-TV and KIII-TV, the demolition is expected to take about 130 days once work begins at the site. The decision follows several failed plans to redevelop the building. Recent engineering studies estimated that restoring it could cost as much as $120 million.Decades of vacant decay and failed redevelopmentThe courthouse, built in the classical revival style, served as Nueces County's main administrative and judicial building for more than six decades. County operations moved to a modern facility nearby in 1977. Since then, the building at 1100 North Mesquite Street has remained empty. Over the years, it has suffered serious weather damage, structural decay and environmental problems. Official documents submitted to the Corpus Christi Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone Board (TIRZ #3) describe several unsuccessful attempts to save the building. The county tried to sell the property to private developers on three separate occasions. One major effort began in May 2018. County officials and the TIRZ #3 Board worked on a plan to turn the historic courthouse into a luxury boutique hotel under the "Le Méridien" brand. The project included a $1 million municipal tax incentive. However, private developers eventually withdrew after detailed financial studies showed that repairing the structure, cleaning up environmental hazards and meeting modern building codes would make the project too expensive to be financially viable. Later efforts to work with the Texas Historical Commission's Town Square Initiative also failed. The partnerships could not secure enough private funding to cover the large gap between the property's value and the cost of renovation.Funding structure and legal approvalsTo pay for clearing the neglected property, Nueces County secured up to $2 million in tax increment reinvestment funding from the City of Corpus Christi. Under an agreement approved by the TIRZ #3 Board in January 2026, the city will repay the county through three annual payments of $666,666. The payments will follow verified completion of the demolition work. Before demolition could be scheduled, county officials also had to deal with legal restrictions on the property. The site was covered by a historic preservation agreement enforced by the Texas Historical Commission. The agreement was set to remain in place through 1 September 2027. Nueces County commissioners worked directly with state officials to change the deed restrictions. This cleared the way for the county to obtain building permits and proceed with demolition.Salvage operations and historical preservationAlthough heavy machinery will eventually tear down the main building, county leaders have confirmed that they will document the site and save historical items where it is safe to do so. During a meeting of the Commissioners Court, local officials said they needed to balance historic preservation with serious health risks inside the damaged building. County leaders explained that historical records, books and selected architectural features would be catalogued. However, widespread asbestos contamination in the plaster and insulation limits what can safely be removed and stored. "We have to make a book and we have to preserve some of the things like that," Nueces County official Chesney said in remarks reported by KIII-TV. "But a lot of that stuff also has asbestos in it. So we have to be really careful in what we keep, because we don't want to keep things that are going to harm people." Selected exterior plaques, stonework that is free of contamination and commemorative statues will be moved to local historical archives or used in future public displays.Future development of the downtown parcelDemolishing the 1914 courthouse is expected to make valuable land available for future development. The property sits directly beside the new Harbor Bridge corridor leading into downtown Corpus Christi. After the vote, county officials said the cleared land would become part of a wider planning process involving local government agencies, the City of Corpus Christi and the Port of Corpus Christi. Removing the empty building will eliminate a long-standing source of urban decay and safety risks. It will also reduce the ongoing security costs paid by county taxpayers. With the $1.3 million demolition contract approved and funding commitments in place, contractors are preparing to access the site and establish safety measures to contain asbestos during removal. articles.title: Malibu wildfire rages, triggering evacuations in Southern California
articles.summary: A blaze in Malibu known as the Bryson Fire has triggered evacuations in the famed Southern California beach community, and the weather will provide little relief over the weekend.
articles.body: A blaze in Malibu known as the Bryson Fire has triggered evacuations in the famed Southern California beach community, and the weather will provide little relief over the weekend. Critical fire conditions are expected to persist as a threatening combination of strong Santa Ana winds, low humidity and dry vegetation will make it more difficult to contain wildfires in the region, Los Angeles County officials said Friday. Firefighters worked overnight to suppress the wildfire that broke out late Thursday afternoon in western Malibu, managing to contain 17% of the Bryson Fire as of Friday morning, said Lindsey P. Horvath, supervisor of the Los Angeles County’s third district. “It is still red flag alert,” Horvath said in a press conference Friday morning, adding that such conditions are expected to last at least until Saturday night. “Be vigilant and be prepared.” The Bryson Fire began just before 5 p.m. on Thursday on Encinal Canyon Road’s rugged terrain in the Santa Monica Mountains. The fire is currently at 146 acres, Los Angeles County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said Friday. No fatalities and no structure losses or damages have been reported as of Friday morning. Marrone said he estimates that more than a hundred structures in the general area of the Bryson Fire are threatened. “If the winds kick up later this afternoon, and we were to lose containment of the fire, a larger area could be affected and under threat,” Marrone said. Evacuation orders for the Encinal, Trancas and Zuna Canyon areas have been issued, meaning residents must leave immediately as they face an immediate threat to life and property because of the Bryson Fire. So far, the Red Cross has set up one emergency shelter at Agoura High School for evacuees who need a place to stay. As of early Friday afternoon, a dozen evacuation warnings have been issued in the immediate areas surrounding the Encinal, Trancas and Zuna canyons — alerting residents to prepare to leave their homes at a moment’s notice. At least one firefighter sustained minor injuries from working to contain the fire Thursday night. That person was transported to a hospital and is expected to recover, Marrone said. Over 400 firefighters are continuing to work on containing the Bryson Fire assigned to this incident alongside more than 75 “ground and aerial resources committed,” Marrone said. Winds from up to 35 mph are expected to heighten fire weather threats in the area, according to the National Weather Service, with gusts forecast to reach up to 70 mph. These conditions could potentially help spark new fires or allow existing fires to rapidly spread. The risk for fires will be highest on Friday for western Los Angeles County, Ventura County and southeastern Santa Barbara County. “As wildfires continue to burn faster and push deeper into our built environment, I urge residents to continue to monitor high-risk weather conditions,” Marrone said. Hours before the Bryson Fire began Thursday, another wildfire erupted in the city of Azusa, located north of Los Angeles. The Peak Fire burned 43 acres on Thursday and briefly prompted evacuation orders for a neighborhood in the foothills of the San Gabriel mountains. Forward progress on the blaze had been stopped by Thursday night after firefighter managed to contain 41% of it.

articles.title: In 1834, Edinburgh's oldest Palm House was built; 192 years later, it reopened with its Victorian neighbour after a five-year, £23.5 million restoration that replaced all 5,750 glass panes and returned nearly 600 plants
articles.summary: The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh has officially reopened its two historic Palm Houses after a complex five-year restoration project costing £23.5
articles.body: The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh has officially reopened its two historic Palm Houses after a complex five-year restoration project costing £23.5 million. The work included replacing every single pane of glass in both buildings. The reopening is a major milestone in the garden's 356-year history. It also marks the completion of an important stage in the wider £58 million Edinburgh Biomes development programme. The two glasshouses include the original Octagonal Palm House, built in 1834, and its Victorian neighbour, built in 1858. The Victorian building is recognised as the tallest traditional stone-built Palm House in the world.Extensive architectural and structural repairsTo complete the major repairs, specialists carefully removed and replaced all 5,750 panes of glass across the two buildings. The replacement panes were made using custom templates designed to withstand today's more extreme weather conditions caused by climate change. Along with replacing the glass, contractors repaired 600 square metres of the original Georgian and Victorian iron structures. Restoration teams also completed 500 square metres of careful sandstone repairs. Damaged stonework was replaced with new stones, some weighing up to a quarter of a tonne each. The renovation was funded by the Scottish Government and a major fundraising campaign. According to official announcements from the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, more than £10.6 million was raised through private donations, The National Lottery Heritage Fund and a public appeal that contributed £250,000 to the project.Returning the living collectionBefore construction began in 2021, horticultural experts carefully moved 800 valuable plant specimens from the glasshouses to temporary holding areas elsewhere in the garden. Replanting started earlier this year, with nearly 600 specimens returned to their restored homes. These include rare plants such as the stone gate palm (Trachycarpus princeps). The palm stands more than eight metres tall and is believed to be the largest specimen grown outside China. The collection also includes a ten-year-old sabal palm. It was grown from a seed taken from one of the garden's oldest historical plants, a Sabal mexicana estimated to have been around 200 years old before it was cut down in 2021. To mark the reopening, Gillian Martin MSP, the Scottish Government's Cabinet Secretary for Climate Action and Rural Affairs, joined garden staff to plant the final specimen in the glasshouses. The plant was a Chilean lion plant (Valdivia gayana) grown from a wild source. "For generations the iconic Palm Houses at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh have inspired visitors from Scotland and around the world," Martin said in a statement released by the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. "The restoration of these heritage glasshouses helps to safeguard the globally important plant collections here for the future, ensuring vital work in conservation, education and scientific discovery can continue."Protecting rare and endangered floraThe restored glasshouses provide a vital safe space for vulnerable plants in Scotland's National Botanic Living Collection. The collection includes 13,500 species gathered from 152 countries. Among the rare plants now growing beneath the new glass are the Three Kings vine (Tecomanthe speciosa) from New Zealand, considered one of the rarest wild plants in existence, and the Catkin yew (Amentotaxus argotaenia), a conifer classified as critically endangered. Professor Julia Knights, Regius Keeper at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, highlighted the wider importance of the restoration for global conservation. "As we fight to tackle climate change and nature loss, the reopening of the Palm Houses is a globally significant moment for Scotland and the world," Knights said in a press release issued by the institution. "As well as celebrating our Living Collection of plants, including those endangered in the wild, this moment also reflects our work as Scotland's global scientific centre of excellence in plant science, horticulture, education and conservation." The garden confirmed that visitors must book timed tickets to enter the Palm Houses. The next stage of the Edinburgh Biomes project will focus on upgrading the site's research glasshouses.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Miami high school senior chased a thief after hearing a woman scream; despite being pepper-sprayed, he tackled and restrained the suspect; police have now honoured him with the title ‘Spider-Man of Brickell’
articles.summary: A Miami high school senior who chased down and helped detain a man accused of theft despite being pepper-sprayed has received a hero award from Miami
articles.body: A Miami high school senior who chased down and helped detain a man accused of theft despite being pepper-sprayed has received a hero award from Miami Police for his brave actions, 7News reported.The Good Samaritan, identified as Harry Cossyphas, was on his way to a grocery store in Brickell when he heard a woman shouting ‘robber’ in Spanish. The suspect was allegedly trying to steal her jewellery. He ran after the suspect, followed him into an alley despite being pepper-sprayed, and held him on the ground until police arrived. The incident occurred on 6 August near Southwest 14th Street.Miami Police honoured him with a hero award on Thursday, 15 October, and the department’s officers have started calling him the ‘Spider-Man of Brickell’.An attempted theft and an unexpected heroIt was a regular afternoon. Harry Cossyphas was walking down the street by a bank in Brickell. He was on his way to a grocery store when he heard a woman screaming. Cossyphas did not stop to think it over. He ran after the man. “I started chasing after the suspect. I turned the corner, and I followed him into an alleyway,” the young man told a broadcaster. He chased the alleged thief. Finally, he caught the suspect. That’s when things went south. The suspect spun around, pulled out pepper spray and aimed it at Cossyphas’s left eye.“Then he pulled out pepper spray and started pepper-spraying me,” Cossyphas recalled. It didn’t work. Cossyphas kept going, and the chase carried on until the two reached the Metromover station. When he caught up with the suspect, he brought the man down. Cossyphas believed the man should be behind bars. “I catch up to him, I tackle him, and I hold him on the ground until police arrive on the scene,” he told the channel.A witness, Xio Fermin, who was walking his dog at the scene, recalled the incident. “I’m not sure what he was thinking, but that’s definitely the wrong time. It’s also crazy because this is one of the safest neighbourhoods,” Fermin told The Miami Herald.A video recorded after the confrontation shows bystanders surrounding the suspect as the high school senior holds him on the ground.Spider-Man of BrickellHarry Cossyphas has become a local hero of sorts. Officials were impressed enough to give him a nickname: the ‘Spider-Man of Brickell’. Cossyphas said he had heard other nicknames, too, including ‘Brickell Batman’, and that he liked them all.“It’s a funny one. I’ve heard Brickell Batman, Brickell Spider-Man; they’re all pretty good, so I like those,” he told the station. Miami Police also honoured him for his courage, compassion and responsible decision-making. He was one of 11 students honoured on Thursday, 15 October, by the department and the ‘Do The Right Thing Program’ for their work in the community.Plenty of people have told Cossyphas not to do it again. Citizen’s arrests can be dangerous, and he knows that. But he has no regrets about following his gut. He is simply glad he caught the man. “It was spontaneous; it was a quick decision. I didn’t really have time to think; I just acted. The lady needed help quickly, and I just sprang into action,” he told the outlet. “I really wish I could be helpful and an inspiration to others in my school and the community, and other friends of mine.”Meanwhile, police identified the suspect as 21-year-old Yagiz Dogan. As of late Thursday night, he remained in custody and faced a charge of third-degree grand theft.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pokimane’s China trip takes ‘shocking’ turn after Mimi’s death, best friend’s visa rejection and missing luggage
articles.summary: Twitch streamer Pokimane has shared an update on her life after losing her eight-year-old cat, Mimi.
articles.body: Twitch streamer Pokimane has shared an update on her life after losing her eight-year-old cat, Mimi. In a TikTok video posted on October 15, 2026, Imane Anys spoke about dealing with her loss while facing several problems during a planned trip to Shanghai. Her best friend could not join her because his visa was not approved, and someone took her luggage at the airport. Despite the difficult week, Pokimane said she was trying to stay positive and make the most of her time in China.Pokimane Opens Up About Losing Mimi and Having Her Worst Week EverMimi had been part of Pokimane's life for eight years and was a familiar presence during her streams. The streamer shared the heartbreaking news of her cat's death during an emotional stream on September 28, 2026.According to Pokimane, cleaners had opened the balcony door and left the screen door open. Mimi was able to go outside and fell from the balcony. Pokimane rushed to an emergency veterinarian after learning about the incident, but Mimi could not be saved.She later described the incident as a "heartbreaking, freak accident" and said she did not want to blame anyone.The loss left Pokimane struggling to carry on with her usual routine. About a week later, she spoke about how little she wanted to do anything after losing her pet."I really don't want to get on this plane, but my mom is forcing me to. I've had zero desire to do anything since losing my baby of eight years, Mimi..."In her October 15 TikTok, Pokimane shared more about how she had been feeling. She called it her "worst week ever" and said she was still grieving Mimi's death. She also spoke about feeling stressed and having her period for almost two weeks.A trip with friends had helped her feel better, but the next part of her travel plans did not go as expected. She had spent months planning a visit to Shanghai with her best friend. However, she learned at the last minute that his visa had not been approved. Since her tickets were non-refundable, she decided to travel to China alone.Pokimane Finds a Silver Lining After Someone Takes Her Luggage in ChinaThe problems did not end when Pokimane reached her destination. After landing, she went to collect her luggage and discovered that someone had taken her bag while leaving a similar-looking suitcase behind."To make matters worse, as soon as I landed, I went to grab my luggage and realized someone took my luggage, and I knew someone took it because they left their luggage, which looks exactly like mine."With her pet's loss still weighing on her and her travel plans already changed, the missing luggage added another problem to an already difficult week.However, Pokimane chose to look at things from a different angle. Instead of letting the setbacks ruin her trip, she reminded herself that she still had reasons to feel fortunate."As unlucky as it is, I simply have to laugh because it's so ridiculous, and to be honest, even on my unluckiest day, I know I'm still so fortunate, and that is not lost on me even when things don't go to plan. I always try to find the silver lining. I may not be traveling with my best friend, but I get to spend time with myself and experience solo travel."Pokimane's message showed that she was trying to move forward without ignoring how difficult the past few weeks had been. She was still grieving Mimi, but she also wanted to enjoy the experience of traveling alone.She ended her update by saying she planned to make the most of her trip to China, even though it had turned out very differently from what she expected.You use AI every day. The challenge, known as Spineathlon 2026, raised funds for an appeal to bring advanced spinal imaging equipment to Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital. The proposed EOS scanner is designed to produce detailed images of the spine while reducing radiation exposure compared with conventional X-rays. With £660,000 raised towards an £841,000 target, the campaign aims to improve long-term care for children living with scoliosis.UK hospital team completes six-day fundraising challenge across NorfolkThe challenge, Spineathlon 2026, began on 26 June during Scoliosis Awareness Month. In its second year, the event brought together members of the hospital's spinal surgery team for a journey covering approximately 180 miles, with different forms of travel used across the six-day route.The first stage involved kayaking along the River Yare from Norwich in the direction of Gorleston. The team then continued on foot, travelling from Great Yarmouth to Sea Palling before making their way towards Cromer, Holkham and Hunstanton. The final section took them by bicycle from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King's Lynn back to Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital.The route connected communities across the county while drawing attention to a fundraising appeal for equipment intended to improve care for children and young people who need regular spinal imaging.Money raised through Spineathlon is supporting the N&N Hospitals Charity's Spinal Appeal. Its target is an £841,000 EOS imaging system, a specialist scanner designed to produce detailed images of the spine while substantially reducing radiation exposure compared with conventional X-ray imaging.Why repeated spinal scans matter for childrenScoliosis causes the spine to curve sideways and frequently becomes apparent during childhood or adolescence. Its progression can vary, particularly during periods of rapid growth, so clinicians may need to monitor the shape of the spine over time and assess whether treatment is required.For some young patients, that means returning to hospital for imaging once or twice a year, sometimes more frequently as their condition changes or surgery approaches. Each appointment provides information about the spine's alignment and whether the curve has progressed. The repeated nature of these examinations, however, makes the amount of radiation used an important consideration.Children are more sensitive to radiation than adults, and the cumulative exposure associated with years of monitoring is a concern for patients who require frequent scans. The hospital hopes the proposed EOS system will help reduce that burden without compromising the information doctors need to make decisions about treatment.Consultant spinal surgeon Tom Marjoram said, ““The EOS system can capture images with around an 80% reduction in radiation exposure, which is hugely significant. Children are more vulnerable to radiation, particularly around sensitive areas such as the abdomen and pelvis, so reducing exposure wherever possible is incredibly important.”Imaging system the hospital hopes to bring to the regionThe proposed scanner would be the first EOS system of its kind in the East of England, according to the hospital's appeal. Its potential reach extends beyond Norwich, with children from Norfolk and surrounding areas among those who could benefit.Patients with early-onset scoliosis are one group the equipment could help. Their treatment and monitoring may begin at a particularly young age, leaving them facing repeated imaging throughout childhood. Children whose spinal curves change quickly during growth spurts can also require close observation.The system is intended to give the spinal team clearer information while reducing the radiation involved in obtaining it. Better imaging can help clinicians understand a patient's condition, follow changes and plan interventions where necessary. The hospital's fundraising effort is therefore focused on acquiring a specific piece of clinical equipment rather than supporting a general expansion of services.At £841,000, the target represents a substantial fundraising commitment. The £660,000 raised for the appeal marks considerable progress, although further money is needed before the hospital reaches the full amount required for the system.How scoliosis affected Scarlett Turrell’s confidence and daily lifeScarlett Turrell, a 19-year-old trainee dental nurse from Lowestoft, has received treatment for scoliosis and has spoken about the experience of being diagnosed and monitored. Her account illustrates how the condition can affect everyday life as well as lead to repeated hospital appointments.She recalled that clothing became a particular source of insecurity after her diagnosis, with the condition affecting her confidence. The early stages of treatment involved several scans while clinicians assessed her spine. She later attended for monitoring once or twice a year, with appointments becoming more frequent as she approached surgery.For young people, scoliosis can involve more than the medical questions surrounding the degree of curvature and the possibility of an operation. Changes in posture and body shape can influence how they feel about their appearance, while the need for continuing assessments becomes part of their routine. Access to imaging that reduces radiation exposure could address one aspect of that experience, even though it does not remove the need for treatment or follow-up.Schools and local groups are being asked to helpThe N&N Hospitals Charity has encouraged schools, businesses, community organisations and individuals to contribute to the Spinal Appeal. Suggested activities include non-uniform days, bake sales, sponsored events and other local fundraising initiatives.The range of activities means that support need not depend on taking part in a challenge as demanding as Spineathlon. Community groups can organise smaller events, while businesses and individuals can make donations towards the equipment fund.With £660,000 raised against the £841,000 target, the appeal still needs additional contributions to reach its goal. The hospital's six-day journey across Norfolk has helped bring attention to that shortfall and to the needs of children who depend on regular spinal imaging.You use AI every day. articles.body: TOI correspondent from London: Indian national Deepak Sandhu, who came to the UK on a student visa, was on Friday sent to jail for life with a minimum of 28 years for murdering a Chinese woman he met at a brothel.It took a jury at the Old Bailey just two hours to convict Sandhu (24) of murdering Chinese national Xiaoqing Ke (39), who he met at a brothel in Southampton where he was a customer and she was working. He was also convicted of perverting the course of justice. Sandhu denied the charges. He was thrown off his IT course at Southampton Solent University and his visa was revoked six months later for poor attendance; he was actually working as a casual labourer on building sites.After Xiaoqing discovered that Sandhu had been lying and had stolen £500 from her handbag, she ended the relationship in Aug 2025.Sandhu pestered Xiaoqing and persuaded her to meet by promising to repay her money. In reality he wanted revenge, the court was told.Doorbell camera footage from Xiaoqing’s Airbnb captured him arriving with his face wrapped in a scarf and leaving after about 90 minutes. Police discovered her body the following day. articles.title: In 1899, Indianapolis built a dam to create a boating lake on the White River; 127 years later, crews are removing it after the structure altered more than four miles of river and blocked aquatic wildlife
articles.summary: Indianapolis has begun removing the Emrichsville Dam from the White River, ending more than a century of disruption to the river’s natural flow and
articles.body: Indianapolis has begun removing the Emrichsville Dam from the White River, ending more than a century of disruption to the river’s natural flow and aquatic habitats. According to The Indianapolis Star, the project is intended to improve conditions for wildlife and make the waterway safer for people. The US Fish and Wildlife Service and the environmental organisation Discover White River have also outlined the ecological benefits of restoring fish passage and reconnecting river habitats. The Emrichsville Dam was constructed in 1899, just south of 16th Street in Indianapolis, as part of efforts to develop a boating area known as Lake Indy near Riverside Park. The project was intended to support recreational activities rather than provide flood control or serve as a primary source of public water.The structure stretches approximately 250 feet across the West Fork of the White River. Its construction changed the river’s natural conditions for around 4.3 miles upstream, affecting water movement and creating a barrier for aquatic species. The dam partially collapsed in October 2018, prompting emergency repairs that involved placing rocks in the river to manage the remaining structure. Although the repairs addressed immediate concerns, the barrier continued to affect wildlife movement and posed safety risks for people using the river.Why removing the dam matters for wildlifeDams can interrupt the movement of fish between feeding grounds, spawning areas and seasonal habitats. Removing the Emrichsville Dam will allow aquatic animals to travel more freely along the White River, helping restore connections between habitats. The benefits extend beyond fish. Freshwater mussels, several species of which are threatened or imperilled in Indiana, depend on fish to transport their larvae to new locations. When fish cannot move freely through a river system, the reproductive cycles and distribution of these mussels can also be affected. Restoring the river’s connectivity could therefore support a wider range of aquatic species and help improve the resilience of the ecosystem. The US Fish and Wildlife Service has identified unrestricted fish passage and ecological restoration as key objectives of the project.Funding the restoration projectThe Indianapolis Department of Public Works is leading the removal, supported by funding from the US Fish and Wildlife Service, the Indiana Department of Natural Resources and The Nature Conservancy. The federal contribution includes a $750,000 grant awarded through the National Fish Passage Program. The initiative supports projects that remove or bypass barriers to aquatic movement and restore access to upstream habitats. Since 1999, the programme has helped remove or bypass more than 3,400 barriers and reopen access to over 61,000 miles of upstream habitat across the United States, according to the federal agency.Historic structures to remainWhile the project will remove the dam’s in-stream components, not every part of the site will disappear. Indianapolis officials decided to preserve the two historic towers on either bank following discussions with historic preservation agencies. One of the towers is locally known as the Beer Tower. The decision allows the city to address the dam’s environmental and safety concerns while retaining elements of the site’s history.Removal work is expected to conclude on December 18, 2026, with additional administrative and related work scheduled to continue into February 2027. After construction, the city plans to monitor the river’s ecosystem, water movement and flow for a year to assess the effects of the restoration. The project marks a shift in how Indianapolis manages this stretch of the White River, moving away from a structure built for recreational purposes in the 19th century towards a river corridor designed to support wildlife movement, safer recreation and a healthier aquatic ecosystem.You use AI every day. articles.title: After his infant daughter underwent heart surgery in 1996, Sylvester Stallone donated $200,000 to help other children with heart defects
articles.summary: When Sylvester Stallone’s infant daughter, Sophia Rose Stallone, underwent surgery for a congenital heart defect in November 1996, the experience brought
articles.body: When Sylvester Stallone’s infant daughter, Sophia Rose Stallone, underwent surgery for a congenital heart defect in November 1996, the experience brought the actor face to face with the challenges families endure when their children need specialised medical care. Sophia was diagnosed with a hole in her heart, which doctors at UCLA Medical Center successfully corrected. In January 1998, Stallone channelled that personal experience into a charitable effort, donating $200,000 to the Heart of a Child Foundation to support research into congenital heart defects. Part of the money came from sales of T-shirts he designed for Planet Hollywood, the restaurant chain he co-owned. His contribution helped support an organisation established by families who wanted to advance research and improve treatment for children with heart conditions.Sophia Stallone’s heart surgery in 1996Sophia Rose Stallone, the eldest daughter of Sylvester Stallone and Jennifer Flavin, was born on August 27, 1996. Doctors discovered that she had a congenital heart defect described in contemporary reports as a hole in her heart.In November 1996, Sophia underwent surgery at UCLA Medical Center in Los Angeles. The procedure was performed by Dr Hillel Laks, then chief of cardiothoracic surgery at the hospital. The operation was successful, and Sophia recovered.The experience gave Stallone a personal connection to families whose children require specialised cardiac treatment. His daughter’s recovery subsequently motivated him to support research into congenital heart defects and help improve the prospects of other young patients.Stallone donated $200,000 to the Heart of a Child FoundationIn January 1998, Stallone presented a $200,000 cheque to the Heart of a Child Foundation at Planet Hollywood in Beverly Hills. Dr Laks accepted the cheque on behalf of the organisation.The foundation was established in 1997 by families who had experienced the loss of children to congenital heart defects. They wanted to support research into the causes of these conditions and help advance treatment for affected children.Jeffrey Bronchick, one of the founders, told the Los Angeles Times in January 1998 that the families had struggled to find an organisation specifically dedicated to research into congenital heart defects. The foundation was created to address that need by directing funding towards medical research.Stallone’s donation supported this mission, drawing on the experience of his daughter’s successful treatment to help advance a cause affecting thousands of families.How T-shirt sales helped raise the moneyStallone helped generate funds for the contribution by designing special T-shirts sold exclusively through Planet Hollywood restaurants. Proceeds from the sales contributed to the $200,000 donation.The initiative combined his creative work with his involvement in the restaurant business. Planet Hollywood, known for its entertainment-themed restaurants and celebrity connections, provided a platform for selling the merchandise and raising money for paediatric heart research.The fundraising effort gave customers an opportunity to contribute to the cause while purchasing merchandise associated with the actor. It also demonstrated how Stallone used his commercial ventures to support a charitable organisation focused on children’s health.The foundation’s mission to help children with heart defectsThe Heart of a Child Foundation was established to support research into congenital heart defects, which develop before birth and can affect the structure or functioning of the heart.Some of these conditions require surgery or other medical interventions during infancy. Research into their causes, along with improvements in diagnosis and treatment, is important for helping affected children receive appropriate care.The foundation’s founders brought personal experience to the effort, having faced the loss of children to congenital heart conditions. Their goal was to direct resources towards research and improve the treatment available to other families.Stallone’s contribution supported the organisation during its early years, when its founders were working to establish a dedicated source of funding for paediatric cardiac research.Stallone and Jennifer Flavin supported a later fundraiserStallone and his wife, Jennifer Flavin Stallone, continued their involvement with the foundation after the 1998 donation.In May 1999, the couple participated in a fashion-show fundraiser at a St John boutique in Beverly Hills. Reported by the Los Angeles Times in June that year, the event attracted more than 150 people and raised over $10,000 for the Heart of a Child Foundation.Flavin Stallone modelled clothing alongside Deanna Martin, the daughter of entertainer Dean Martin. The event brought together fashion and fundraising to support the foundation’s work on congenital heart defects.Turning a family experience into support for othersSophia’s recovery after heart surgery became a turning point in Stallone’s charitable involvement with paediatric heart health. His $200,000 donation helped support a foundation created by families seeking better research and treatment for children with congenital heart defects.The contribution also brought together his personal experience and his work with Planet Hollywood, with T-shirt sales helping raise funds for the cause. The subsequent fundraiser involving Stallone and Flavin extended their support beyond the original cheque presentation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Oregon school shooting: Meet Kaylub Giamanco, 36-year-old carpenter and father of two hailed as hero after stopping deadly attack at Silver Rail Elementary School
articles.summary: A father of two who was driving home during his lunch break rushed into an Oregon elementary school after hearing gunshots and confronted a teenage gunman
articles.body: A father of two who was driving home during his lunch break rushed into an Oregon elementary school after hearing gunshots and confronted a teenage gunman who had opened fire inside the building. Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter from Bend, Oregon, has been credited with stopping the attack at Silver Rail Elementary School.According to a report by The New York Post, which spoke to Giamanco’s mother, Kenda Freeman, the father is not seeking public recognition and his family has asked for privacy. His brother, Kyle Giamanco, also told NBC News that Kaylub is struggling with the aftermath of the tragedy and reportedly feels guilty that he could not save more lives.The shooting claimed the lives of three children, aged 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher. Another student, aged seven, and a 54-year-old teacher were critically injured, according to the report.Who is Kaylub Giamanco?According to his brother’s account to NBC News, Giamanco was heading home from his lunch break at around 1 pm on Thursday when he heard gunfire coming from the school area. His two daughters attend Silver Rail Elementary.Giamanco, who owns a concealed firearm, reportedly followed the gunman into the school’s special-education room and fatally shot him, his brother said. articles.title: 73+ brands dropped new products this month — these are the ones our editors already love from Away, Kindle and more
articles.summary: Shopping experts tested new products from Samsung, Kindle, Hoka, Nutrafol, Oofos and more this month. These are brands’ best launches of October across categories.
articles.body: This story is part of NBC Selected’s New & Notable column, where we highlight our favorite product launches. We will continuously update this article throughout the month with new releases we think you should know about. Footwear, apparel and accessories launches Podiatrists we’ve talked to say the Hoka Arahi is one of their favorite stability sneakers for walking and running, and the brand just debuted its latest version. The Arahi 9, which is made with a little more cushioning for a slightly softer feel compared to the previous iteration, has Hoka’s H-frame stability system to prevent your feet from overpronating (rolling inward too much). The brand upgraded the material on the sides of the shoe, making it tighter to give you more support, and added reflective details for extra safety in low light. You can get these sneakers in men’s and women’s sizes, and regular, wide and extra-wide widths. Nike created these shoes for people who cross-train, meaning they run and strength train back-to-back — for example, they’re ideal for CrossFit, Orangetheory or Hyrox. The sneakers, which come in men’s and women’s styles, have enough cushioning to absorb shock and keep your feet comfortable while running, but not so much that you feel unstable while lifting. Their wide base gives your feet lots of contact with the ground to stay balanced, there’s rubber at the heel to prevent the foam from expanding too much during weighted exercises and the grippy, durable outsole makes sure your feet stay in place. The Hybrid RN also has an X-shaped overlay on the top of the shoe to secure your feet as you quickly switch moves. These Oofos slippers blend recovery with coziness. They’re made with the brand’s signature foam and deep heel cup to absorb impact and keep you comfortable with every step, plus there’s a shearling lining for added warmth. “My feet are chronically achy and standing at the kitchen sink or stove leaves my back sore, too — these mules help ease that,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman. “I wear them around the house and outside, and since they slip on and off easily, they’re perfect for my son’s shoes-off mommy-and-me gym class or a quick trash run. I also like that the fur feels stylish for fall.” More notable apparel and footwear launches Dairy Boy Playful Traditions CollectionDaphne The Everything Shower Collection: The House Cat Robe, The House Cat Wrap, The Hair Towel, The Spa Headband, The Sleepy Robe, The Eyemask and The Hannah DusterUgg Vanley SneakerUniqlo x JW Anderson CollectionUgg x JW Anderson Collection Tech launches The new 6-inch Kindle is Amazon’s most pocket-sized e-reader yet. A seamless flush-front design makes it lighter, while 16GB of storage, up to six weeks of battery life and 30 percent faster book opening keep you reading uninterrupted. It’s made with recycled materials and a 100 percent recycled cobalt battery. You can also upgrade to a 32GB aluminum-back version with a premium matte finish. Along with this new 6-inch Kindle, Amazon just launched a new version of the Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Papersoft, which are currently available for pre-order with shipping starting October 28. The Alexa Tablet 11 is Amazon’s new mid-size tablet, built around Alexa+ and wrapped in aluminum. Its 11-inch, 2.5K display runs at a smooth 90Hz and reaches 500 nits, making it well suited to streaming, browsing and reading. Inside, an octa-core MediaTek processor and 8GB of RAM keep things responsive, with 64GB or 128GB of storage. Dolby Atmos stereo speakers, dual microphones, a fingerprint sensor, Wi-Fi 6 and IP52 splash resistance round out the tablet. The battery delivers up to 15 hours of video or up to 20 hours of reading, according to the brand. You can also add an optional magnetic stylus for notes and sketches. This device is part of an entirely new slate of Amazon tablets, including the bigger-screen Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the smaller, more affordable Alexa Tablet 8 and new kids tablets. Samsung’s latest tablet has a 14.6-inch screen, faster processing, upgraded overall performance and a longer-lasting battery life, making it ideal for enjoying entertainment, making video calls and treating it as a laptop substitute. “I’ve been testing this for a few weeks and I’m amazed by how good movies and television shows look on it,” says Heitman. “It’s also fast and smooth, meaning that switching between apps never feels sluggish.” The tablet, which launched alongside the smaller and lighter Tab S12+, also has multi-window view and comes with a stylus, and apps for creators like Adobe Photoshop and Pinterest come pre-loaded. There’s built-in smart helpers too, like Note Assist, which can tidy up your notes and pull out the key points for you. Meet Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta’s first audio-only AI glasses. With no camera or display, they’re the lightest and slimmest pair in the lineup, looking like classic Ray-Bans in Clubmaster and Burbank styles. Open-ear speakers let you stream music, podcasts and calls without earbuds, while built-in microphones give you hands-free access to Meta AI, including live translation. Enjoy up to 12 hours of battery life, and there’s prescription-lens options. Meta also recently announced that it’s adding Muse, a personal AI agent, to its AI glasses, and it debuted the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, which has better battery life and a slimmer, more comfortable design compared to the previous iteration, plus a customizable action button. You can also now pick from 27 color and lens combinations across three styles. BEMT helps to make formulas lightweight and invisible while still maintaining strong, broad-spectrum UV protection, according to the brand. La Roche-Posay’s new SPF is a revamped version of the original Anthelios formula (which is a tried-and-true NBC Selected favorite) that includes the new ingredient. It has a lightweight texture that absorbs quickly with an invisible finish, making it a great option for all skin tones. It also includes an antioxidant blend that protects skin from environmental and free radical damage for up to 16 hours, and leaves skin hydrated for up to 24, according to the brand. Nutrafol is a favorite among our NBC Selected editors for hair growth, and this serum is the latest launch from the brand with a focus on protecting the hair you already have. The leave-in treatment is meant to reduce breakage and prevent split ends, according to the brand. Plus, it’s lightweight, so it won’t weigh down your hair. “I like to style my hair with a blow dryer brush, which means my hair is full of split ends and breakage,” says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack. “I’ve been using the Strand Serum for the last few weeks and have definitely noticed an improvement in my hair health, which has made styling much easier, and I’ve even noticed that my blowouts are lasting longer.” Hero Cosmetics’ viral pimple patches are some of our favorite ways to cover a breakout and absorb gunk to help them go away. But with the popularity of pimple patches in the shapes of stars, flowers and other cute (and sometimes funky) designs, Hero Cosmetics has finally adopted the trend with these newly released patches. They’re kicking off with a limited-edition, holiday-themed collection, including patches in the form of peppermints, snowflakes and more. It has interchangeable blades that let you dice, chop, slice, shred and puree, and then you can take off the PowerPod motor and serve everything inside the tool. It also comes with covers to store the food. To use the Prepi, you add whole ingredients to the chute and press down on them with the plunger, guiding them through the blade. Other than the blade, all parts are dishwasher-safe. Most of Windmill’s home appliances are designed to keep you cool — until now. The brand’s newest product is a space heater that oscillates to distribute warmth across rooms and reduce cold spots. It operates quietly and has three heat settings, a timer, an auto-dimming display, a handle and a compact design that’s not an eyesore in your home. Plus, you don’t need an app to use it — just adjust its settings with the included remote. The space heater also has numerous built-in safety features: The plug monitors heat levels and disconnects the power if needed; there’s overheat and tip-over protection; the internal components are VO flame-retardant; you can turn on a child safety lock; and there’s a plugged-in warning light. This coffee maker replicates the pour-over brewing method: It manually pours hot water in a spiral pattern over a filter with ground coffee at timed internals, which makes for an extra flavorful cup of joe. It has a built-in grinder that prepares coffee so it’s perfect for pour over, as well as a delayed auto start option. There are also customizable features, letting you adjust temperature, strength and grind type, for example. You can brew directly into mugs for smaller single-serve cups or brew into the 20-ounce carafe to make enough for a crowd. More notable home and kitchen launches Baby Brezza ProWash360 Bottle Washer, Sterilizer and DryerCoway Airmega Mighty2 Mini Air PurifierHexClad Hybrid Bakeware SetKitchenAid Go Cordless Grater, Slicer, Shredder and Handheld Vacuum Sealer Starter Pack Oster Vortex BlenderPiecework Pillow CollectionRuggable Easy Care Wool CollectionSteamery Pilo Core Fabric ShaverS’well Glass+ CollectionUgg Pet CollectionKeurig Alta System (sold out — sign up to learn about restocks) Travel launches Away’s iconic luggage just got an upgrade. The Series 3 collection has multiple new features to make travel seamless, including a built-in wheel brake that keeps your suitcase in place, a hook (on the handle) to hang an extra item like a jacket or duty-free bag, a dedicated pocket for your Bluetooth tracker and smoother, quieter wheels. The handle also adjusts to lock anywhere you want it; no more three-level height limits. Both sides of the suitcases also now open outward, making it easier to see everything packed inside, and they come with the brand’s compression system to fit as much of your stuff as possible These new features will be available across Away’s classic styles (Carry-On 3, Bigger Carry-On 3, Medium 3, Large 3, and Trunk 3) and expandable Flex styles (Carry-On Flex 3, Bigger Carry-On Flex 3, Medium Flex 3 and Large Flex 3). Away also launched its Signature Bags collection this month with five new styles: the Signature Companion Bag (which you can use as your in-flight personal item), Signature Tote, Signature Triple Zip Duffle (part briefcase, part duffel bag), Signature Weekender and Slim Commuter Backpack. The Bogg Bag is one of the most popular beach bags on the market, and after making dozens of versions and accessories, the brand now offers an additional bag: the Go Tote. It’s a lightweight everyday bag made from soft, flexible, water-resistant, easy-to-clean material. The Go Tote has a flat, durable, tip-resistant base, just like the original Bogg Bag, as well as top handles and a crossbody strap. There’s internal and external pockets for all your stuff, too. You can get the bag in three sizes: Go Little, Go Tote and Go Big. After shutting down in 2025, Paravel is officially under new ownership and back with a suite of travel essentials. You can now shop some of its most popular, recently refreshed pieces, like the hard-shell Aviator Luggage in four sizes (carry-on, carry-on plus, grand and trunk) and the Signature Canvas Totes. There’s also travel accessories: a set of four packing cubes and a luggage tag. The Tread Flex is quiet and folds up, making it ideal for smaller spaces. The Tread Vision has a cushioned belt and built-in camera that tracks your movement and offers tips. Then there is the top-of-the-line Tread+ Vision, which features a cushioned belt, extra room to run and a mode that allows you to turn it into a strength-building sled. All three also have a swiveling HD touchscreen, personalized training plans and smart pace suggestions. Period care brand Thinx expanded into apparel for the first time with these flowy, athletic-inspired shorts that have built-in, leak-resistant period underwear. There’s an absorbent gusset on the inside of the shorts, so you can wear them day and night for up to 12 hours. They’re made from breathable mesh and have a stretchy waistband, which is ideal for workouts, running errands and travel. articles.title: 'The View' co-hosts cast doubt on Kamala Harris viability as 2028 candidate
articles.summary: "The View" co-hosts debated former Vice President Kamala Harris' 2028 prospects, with Sara Haines pointing to the public's desire for fresher Democratic candidates
articles.body: Several co-hosts of "The View" expressed doubts Friday about former Vice President Kamala Harris running for president in 2028. Harris was asked during a Tuesday interview with podcaster Keke Palmer whether she was considering running for president in 2028. Harris laughed and said she hadn't decided yet. However, some of "The View" co-hosts urged the Democratic Party to seek another contender. "Let’s be real," co-host Ana Navarro said, noting that she spoke with Harris about how many women remain "scarred" by the fact both she and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton lost to President Donald Trump. When asked if a Black woman could be elected president, guest host Raven-Symone replied, "Not in America. In the days after Joe Biden dropped out in 2024, online platforms saw racist content directed at Kamala go up 525% and misogynistic content went up 2,328%." DEMOCRATS DEBATE KAMALA HARRIS 2028 RUN AS SURROGATE SAYS PARTY WANTS TO 'MOVE ON' FROM 2024 LOSS "We are not as progressive as we think we are, United States," Raven-Symone added. "There are other countries doing it much better when it comes to women in office. You need to catch the blank up, period." "If the Democrats want to win, but I don’t think she is the right candidate," Sara Haines said. "Because the Democrats have been screaming for new energy, that they would need something new to combat this. This would be her third time on this ballot from the first time when she didn’t — she was out really early when she ran, and then the time with Biden, this would be the third time." "People are clamoring for fresh energy and there is a lot of candidates – Pete Buttigieg, Mark Kelly, [Josh] Shapiro, Wes Moore. They’re moderate, moderate Democrats and I think they could sweep," Haines said, later noting that Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., would be viable down the road as well. JOY BEHAR DOUBLES DOWN ON ARGUMENT US WILL NOT ELECT A WOMAN PRESIDENT Democratic strategist and co-host of "The Huddle" podcast Dan Turrentine told Fox News Digital, "I think America is ready for a female president. The two women who have lost were politically flawed, and it was known from the beginning." "For Harris in 2028, the challenge is that candidates that have successfully run three times — Reagan, Trump — were ideologically consistent, and the country came to them. Harris has been inconsistent, creating an authenticity problem," he continued. "You then have to look at the present dynamic of the Democratic Party — angry and demanding fight. Harris has been MIA the last two years, which is consistent with her history of caution and indecision," Turrentine said. "Lastly, if Harris runs, she will have to fight an establishment and media that are very skeptical and will likely look to pounce," he added. "There are a lot of reasons to question her chances. But, if she runs, she will be a serious candidate in the primary, and if she were to win the primary, in this bitterly divided country, would start the general with a decent chance." articles.title: Built in 1831, New Jersey’s Morris Canal used 23 water-powered inclined planes to move boats up and down 100 feet in 15 minutes
articles.summary: In 1824, the Morris Canal & Banking Company was chartered to build a canal carrying Pennsylvania coal to markets along the eastern seaboard.
articles.body: In 1824, the Morris Canal & Banking Company was chartered to build a canal carrying Pennsylvania coal to markets along the eastern seaboard. The Canal Society of New Jersey says the waterway opened in 1831 and relied on 23 lift locks and 23 water-powered inclined planes. According to the American Society of Civil Engineers, the inclined planes were essentially short railways that let boats change as much as 100 feet in elevation in 15 minutes. The canal climbed 914 feet from Newark Bay to Lake Hopatcong, then dropped 760 feet to the Delaware River at Phillipsburg.Why did the Morris Canal use 23 inclined planes and 23 locksAccording to the Canal Society of New Jersey, the canal stretched 102 miles from Phillipsburg on the Delaware River to Jersey City, overcoming the rugged terrain of the state's highlands. It states that engineers had to manage an elevation change of 1,674 feet. The total length was 106 miles. The canal climbed 914 feet from Newark Bay to the summit at Lake Hopatcong, then dropped 760 feet to the Delaware River at Phillipsburg. This gave the canal an average vertical slope of 18 feet per mile. This was steep compared with the Erie Canal's relatively gentle slope of one foot per mile.The hydraulic-powered inclined plane system was "the key civil engineering feature" that permitted the canal's successful completion in 1831. It states that the system consisted of 23 hydraulically powered inclined planes, used in combination with 23 locks. The locks handled elevation changes of 12 feet or less, and the inclined planes accomplished the remaining grade changes.The inclined planes were essentially short railways. They allowed canal boats to change as much as 100 feet in elevation in 15 minutes. The Canal Society of New Jersey likewise states that the canal's 23 lift locks and 23 water-powered inclined planes could raise or lower boats up to 100 feet at a time. It describes these structures as making the canal an engineering triumph of its era.What goods did boats carry on the Morris Canal during its peak operationMule-drawn boats capable of carrying up to 70 tons of cargo navigated the canal in five days. During its peak, it states, hundreds of boats transported coal, iron ore and agricultural products. The Society describes the canal as "New Jersey's first industrial transportation system" and says it reshaped the region's economy.The canal had become obsolete by the early 1900s because of advances in railroads and other transportation systems. It states that the canal was officially dismantled in 1924. Ownership of its water resources, including Lake Hopatcong, Lake Musconetcong and Greenwood Lake, passed to the State of New Jersey. The Society adds that the Morris Canal Greenway, led by the Canal Society and local communities, now works to preserve the canal's remains through interpretation, public education and recreational opportunities.You use AI every day.
